thread.title: Dow looks likely to cling to 26,000 threshold, but bulls take a breather

author: Barbara Kollmeyer
title: Dow looks likely to cling to 26,000 threshold, but bulls take a breather
text:
U.S. stock futures pointed to a flat start for Thursday, with the Dow industrials set to hover near their record 26,000-plus level. Another strong run looked doubtful for now as investors grew wary of the potential for a partial government shutdown.
Quarterly earnings results will roll out from financials such as Morgan Stanley, while weekly jobless claims and housing starts will also be in focus.
What are the main benchmarks doing? 
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures YMH8, +0.05% were up 3 points to 26,100, while S&P 500 futures ESH8, +0.04% slipped 0.45 point to 2,803.50. Nasdaq-100 futures NQH8, -0.06% fell 9.5 points, or 0.1%, to 6,814.
All three major indexes closed at all-time highs on Wednesday , driven by optimism over the economy and corporate results. Leading the pack, the Dow DJIA, +1.25% rallied 332.79 points to close at 26,115.65, the first finish ever above 26,000. The S&P 500 SPX, +0.94% rose 0.9% to 2,802.56. The Nasdaq Composite Index COMP, +1.03% rose 1% to 7,298.28.
What’s driving markets? 
Optimism over the economy and earnings have helped fuel gains in the new year, with the week already delivering a more than 1% advance for the Dow. However, investors may be looking to catch their breath from that run, with some reluctance to push the market higher ahead of a crucial next few days in politics. 
Lawmakers are working to carve out a deal to avoid a looming shutdown for Saturday. The two main political parties looked to be making little headway though, with immigration a major sticking point. Republican leaders are scheduled to bring forward a short-term spending bill to keep the government running through mid-February, The Wall Street Journal reported. 
Read: Government shutdowns haven’t always been so bad for Wall Street stocks 
Which stocks look like key movers? 
Morgan Stanley MS, +1.37% and Bank of New York Mellon Corp. BK, +0.61% are among the companies due to report ahead of the bell on Thursday. IBM Corp. IBM, +2.93% and American Express Co. AXP, +0.42% are scheduled to report after the bell. 
Shares of aluminum producer Alcoa Corp. AA, +1.33% slumped 6.6% in thin premarket trade after quarterly results missed Wall Street forecasts . 
Kinder Morgan Inc. KMI, +0.93% could follow late-session gains Wednesday after the oil and gas infrastructure group’s earnings beat forecasts . 
Apple Inc. AAPL, +1.65% shares could remain in focus as investors digest a series of plans announced Wednesday celebrated as promises to hire thousands of workers and bring home billions of dollars in cash, but which came under fresh scrutiny .
What are strategists saying? 
“I wouldn’t be surprised if markets made a small retreat, or at least took a breather given the threat of a shutdown this weekend. Avoid a shutdown and much of the enthusiasm for equities will be driven by corporate results which have, so far, been supportive of this rally,” said Lee Wild, head of equity strategy at Interactive Investor, in emailed comments. 
Lee added that the modest moves lower for the Dow are fairly insignificant given the strength of Wednesday’s rally.
What economic data are coming? 
Weekly jobless claims, along with housing starts and building permits for December, are all due out at 8:30 a.m. Eastern Time. The Philadelphia Fed’s manufacturing index for January is due at 10 a.m. Eastern.

Cleveland Fed President Loretta Mester will speak on monetary policy at 6:05 p.m. Eastern. 
What are other assets doing? 
European stocks SXXP, +0.09% were modestly higher, while Asian markets largely gained , lifted by technology stocks. Gold futures GCG8, -0.57% fell as the U.S. Dollar Index DXY, -0.43% traded at almost a one-week high, though it had pared some of those gains early Thursday . 
Oil futures CLG8, +0.03% were flat. Bitcoin BTCUSD, +1.56% moved above $11,000 , a day after a particularly volatile session for cryptocurrencies.
